# Delivery policy contract v1

Explicit `completion_policy: {"schema_version": 1}` adds accepted-scope completion
and protocol-5 activation. Read [the completion contract](COMPLETION_POLICY.md).
Source/export support does not activate existing projects. All keeps unfinished
Merged tasks visible; historical acceptance does not claim Delivered.

Optional [task context](TASK_CONTEXT.md) adds explicit requirements protocol `v2:`
and independent source compatibility under matching execution v2/v3. New scope
ignores only the permitted terminal journal. Old hashes/receipts keep whole-body
meaning; shared delivery fingerprints and actual runtime gates are unchanged.
Outer state 4 fences incompatible writers. Existing activation is a separate
official-config/owned-idle operation; installing this engine grants no adoption.

Execution policy schema 2 keeps this delivery evidence contract and uses
[Approved tasks and frozen batches](BATCH_INTEGRATION.md) for admission/ownership.
Its source PRs target main for independent approval and stay unmerged; only the
reserved combined branch enters configured Stage or main. Stage and promotion include the frozen
batch ID as well as the exact task set. Legacy/v1 routes below remain in force.

The optional [parallel execution contract](PARALLEL_EXECUTION.md) extends this
policy with a repository-wide review/integration owner. In that mode review
evidence also identifies its lane/session, and all tasks (including report-only
work) follow the independently reviewed PR route. Legacy behavior below remains
unchanged when `execution_policy` is absent.

Execution schemas 2/3 also support explicitly disabled staging at a compatible
pin, preserving Approved and all frozen combined-review gates. Read the current
[batch contract](BATCH_INTEGRATION.md#optional-stage-and-authorized-delivery--tt-127).
The direct-main route records a real admitted `main_batches` receipt and never
pretends Stage was tested. Target/completion/required checks remain explicit.

This is an opt-in extension to tracker config schema 3 (also accepted in schema 2).
The Master Repo template generates this block from its project descriptor:

```json
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "staging": {"enabled": true, "branch": "stage", "target": "example/stage"},
  "completion": "verified-production",
  "delivery_target": "example/production",
  "required_checks": ["descriptor", "tracker-link", "tests"]
}
```

Store it as `delivery_policy` in `tracker/config.json`. `project.base_branch` is
main. Completion is `reviewed-merge`, `verified-production` or
`verified-stable-package`. Targets identify actual configured environments or the
local repository, not secrets. Required check names are exact GitHub Actions job
names. The latest run for every required name must pass on the reviewed PR head.
Use one semantic `stage` column between review and merged iff staging is enabled.
The application derives columns from config, not from a universal fixed board.

## Commands and evidence

Use the project client `python scripts/task_tracker.py COMMAND`, or in the engine
checkout `python -m tracker --config PROJECT_CONFIG COMMAND`. Evidence commands
preview by default; add `--apply` to persist. Evidence is written to the project's
existing `tracker-state` branch using the shared compare-and-swap store, not to the
published site. Reports/history/targets are excluded from public task snapshots.
Repository readers can still read the state branch; never place secrets in reports.

1. `check-pr N`: validate links, classifications, route and naming.
2. `record-review --pr N --evidence-file review.json --apply`: record the actual
   independent review after reading it. It must name distinct agent identities,
   current head/base/tree SHAs, verdict and a durable report:

   ```json
   {"kind":"independent-review","implementer":"author-session","reviewer":"review-agent-session",
    "head_sha":"40-hex-sha","base_sha":"40-hex-sha","tree_sha":"40-hex-sha",
    "verdict":"approved","report":"Durable review report reference"}
   ```

   The tool binds this to the task set and policy. Identity strings are an
   attestation by the running agent, not cryptographic proof of independence.
3. `check-merge N`: read-only admission immediately before the GitHub merge.
   The command does not merge. Keep normal GitHub branch protections enabled and
   re-check if the head/base changes. Post-merge commands verify actual Git parents.
4. For staging, merge the source PR, then `stage --pr N --apply`. After actually
   deploying/testing stage, `verify-stage --evidence-file stage.json --apply`:

   ```json
   {"kind":"stage-verification","result":"passed","target":"example/stage",
    "source_sha":"actual-stage-merge-sha","tree_sha":"actual-stage-tree-sha",
    "checks":["Actual smoke/behavior check and result"],"report":"Durable result reference"}
   ```

   `failed` records a failure. A retry of the same candidate preserves its proof;
   a changed candidate needs new proof. Create stage -> main, link the same tasks,
   run `check-merge`, and merge. The main parent and resulting content must match
   the passing stage receipt. No extra product ticket is needed for promotion.
5. `merged EX-12 --pr N --reviewed-complete --apply`: existing completeness and
   ancestry checks plus the new admission evidence. Records Merged only for fully
   delivered code scope; it does not deploy or claim production success.
6. Where delivery is required, run the project's maintained release procedure,
   verify the configured target, then `record-delivery EX-12 --evidence-file
   delivery.json --apply`:

   ```json
   {"kind":"delivery-verification","result":"passed","target":"example/production",
    "merge_shas":["actual-admitted-main-merge-sha"],
    "checks":["Installed version and intended behavior verified"],"report":"Durable result reference"}
   ```

   Use `failed` for a failed attempt. The receipt covers all code merges for each
   supplied task and must match its adopted policy. Repeating merge recording
   preserves an already verified receipt. Release/dependency/UI completion all use
   the same evidence; a Merged label alone cannot bypass it. Non-code `complete`
   still requires its existing Research/Operations classification and verified
   result; it is not an alternative for code implementation.

## New project registration

Export the small client, not the Tracker application:
`export-template --output NEW_DIR --repository owner/repo --name "Project"
--id-prefix EX --base main --engine-revision FULL_SHA --delivery-policy policy.json`.
Run client `init` for project labels. Prepare the shared registry change with
`register-project --workspace workspace.json --project-config NEW_DIR/tracker/config.json
--id example --apply`. Repeating identical registration is safe; conflicts in
identity/prefix/config fail without replacing existing registration. Review and
publish that registry change through the Tracker's maintained release procedure.
Verify the project appears with the expected board and successful fresh sync before
claiming it is connected. A local registry write is not live publication.

## Adoption and compatibility

Do not turn this on implicitly during an engine upgrade. Audit historical IDs,
labels, PRs, completion and release state first. Existing open PRs finish under the
old rules before activation; the migration must report them as blockers. Existing
completed tasks need an explicit evidence reconciliation plan before opting in;
otherwise the stricter policy correctly shows their completion as unverified.
Preserve Issues, release history, custom modules and local deployment controls.
Changing target, checks or completion changes the policy fingerprint, so old proof
cannot authorize a changed policy. Pair any contract change with a Master Repo
impact assessment and a linked compatibility change.

### Staging-only policy migration

`delivery-policy migrate --previous-config ORIGINAL.json --previous-revision
FULL_SHA --report-file cutover.md` previews a narrow staging toggle. It verifies
the exact original config from the official immutable repository revision and
its ancestry to current main. Every non-Stage setting, task identity, execution
capacity, delivery target, completion and required check stays equal. The Stage
target may change to/from the explicitly disabled identity. New configs retain
all historical-completion tasks/provenance, with only that manifest's policy
changed in the explicitly reviewed candidate diff. This command does not edit
config, create approvals or modify Issues/PRs.

Publish compatible engine writers and the single snapshot service before live
adoption. Reserve actual owned maintenance, drain Workers/Reviewers, pending
operations, running intake/batch and unpromoted Stage using their real owners.
Queued Review and Approved entries may remain; the preview verifies their exact
durable queue membership. Preserve the original config and a private state copy.
After the exact reviewed candidate config is published on current main, add
`--apply --actor Maintainer-XXXX --session ACTUAL_RUN --claim MAINTENANCE_ID`.
The operation requires idleness, actual maintenance ownership and shared-file
SHA compare-and-swap. It keeps the fence until supported maintenance resume.
Coordinate writer/config/service agreement before reopening admission.
One preview/apply audit memoizes unchanged read-only GitHub proofs per snapshot
and distinct admitted PR. It checks main again before the write; a concurrent
state change still fails CAS instead of reusing proof across separate commands.

Original delivery receipts and archived batches remain intact. An additive
audited reconciliation binds old/new fingerprints, immutable previous config,
exact current Issue scope, original receipt digest and original admitted main
source/tree identities. Original verification/target/report and pending/failed
state are preserved. Genuine prior success can remain complete under the same
delivery requirements; pending never becomes verified. Changed/reopened scope
cannot borrow the audit. A later actual delivery retains this reconciliation in
history and records fresh current-policy evidence. Reports/claims/reconciliation
details remain private; the public projection contains only the effective policy
and scope digest needed for truthful completion.

Historical pre-batch pending package records may be preserved as unfinished
history instead of being re-admitted as modern batches. The migration recognizes
only the original minimal `policy`/`sources`/`state`/`recorded_at` pending format,
with original official merged stage-to-main PR metadata and no
modern batch/request/admission binding or batch PR marker. Their original receipt
bytes and old policy stay intact; they receive no policy reconciliation, current
delivery authority or completion. The private `retained_legacy_pending` audit
lists each task, original source identities, receipt digest and retention reason.
Legacy v1 review/promotion metadata alone does not make a source a modern batch.
This corroborates only the historical PR identity; it does not reconstruct old
tree/ancestry admission or verify the retained source evidence. Each distinct old
PR metadata read is memoized within this one inspected snapshot.
Any verified/process/non-code record, verification/history/reconciliation data,
known current or archived batch membership, or malformed batch marker retains
the full existing proof requirements. Missing compatible verification is a
reported limitation, never a reason to demote success or silently skip admission.

Closed-completed historical Issues without any status label can remain unchanged
only when they are absent from every durable task/receipt, ownership, queue,
approval, batch/request, historical-completion and retained task-history binding.
Open or tracked work with no status remains an error. No Issue is relabeled,
reopened, archived or made complete. The private `retained_untracked_closed`
audit records the unchanged historical Issue scope and reason, with no admission,
delivery or completion receipt. This retention-only audit is excluded from the
ownership scan on later Stage toggles; genuine task history remains binding.
An old `todo_added` sort timestamp is preserved as non-authoritative metadata;
actual Todo labels, `todo_order`, runs and ownership remain binding. It does not
make a closed historical Issue a current task. Missing or unsupported
identity-container shapes fail closed.

For this bounded operator repair, use a clean independently reviewed merged
TT-129/TT-131 engine checkout with the exact reviewed consumer config and the normal
`delivery-policy migrate` preview/apply commands above. Existing e775-compatible
writers and snapshot readers accept the additive private audit unchanged. No
portable helper, client/config pin or service publication changes for this repair;
permanent engine upgrades remain separate reviewed work. Do not patch a cached
runtime or migrate another consumer merely as a test.

An existing explicit delivery request can also carry through this audit when
its full archived main batch and every exact task receipt reconcile together.
Its original permission/producer/target remains intact; the additive audit binds
the old/new policies, original request digest, main PRs and exact source heads.
This lets the old-route adoption batch finish its already authorized publication
after the new staging policy activates. A missing, cancelled, partial or changed
request is never created or broadened by migration.

Queued Worker handoffs keep their order and owners. Old Approved proof is
preserved as history and cannot enter a new-policy intake. Its recorded
Coordinator uses normal `batch return` to the original author, followed by a
fresh claim/handoff/current-policy independent review/approval; no work is
silently approved or discarded. An already applied migration is idempotent.
Old configs are rejected by the recorded policy marker. Re-enabling Stage uses
the same procedure, including prior Stage reconciliation to current main before
the next batch. Other delivery-policy changes need their own explicit design.

New execution-state adoption records its exact delivery-policy fingerprint.
Preexisting unmarked execution-v2/v3 state predates optional Stage and is accepted
only with its historically supported enabled Stage until the inspected toggle
records that marker. Passing a no-Stage config or combining a delivery change
with execution-capacity migration cannot initialize or bypass it. Genuine old
staged and execution-v1 consumers retain their supported compatibility route.

### Retrospective legacy package confirmation

The separate explicit [`legacy-delivery` operator](LEGACY_DELIVERY_RECONCILIATION.md)
can recover only audited original minimal pending pre-batch records retained by
the genuine staging-only migration. It requires new owner authorization, exact
current task scope, independent full-scope completion and actual official native
signed package installation proof. Migration retention alone grants no authority.
It preserves original producer task scope and original receipts/history and uses
one selected-row CAS without stopping unrelated work. Preview is read-only;
missing evidence or unfinished business acceptance stays pending. This operator
changes no exported helper, ordinary admission/projection or consumer pin.

### Authorized native delivery continuation

After the owner's one integration-and-delivery instruction, the actual
Coordinator uses `batch begin --deliver --delivery-workflow PATH --delivery-job
EXACT_NAME` as documented in the batch contract. Ordinary source/main PRs and
batches created without this request never acquire delivery authorization.
The Coordinator still verifies complete scope and records the real admitted
main merge with ordinary `merged`; an automatic producer cannot approve tasks
or invent this handoff. The project owns the release/deploy, target acceptance,
retry and rollback implementation. Tracker supplies portable request/evidence
validation, not a generic command executor.

The exported recorder needs the same repository token with Actions/Issues read
and contents write, plus the existing portable policy helpers:

```sh
python scripts/tracker_delivery_receipt.py resolve --repository OWNER/REPO \
  --merge-sha MAIN_MERGE_SHA --ci-run SUCCESSFUL_MAIN_CI_RUN --output request.json
python scripts/tracker_delivery_receipt.py record --request request.json \
  --evidence delivery.json --verification-run RUN_ID --verification-job JOB_ID --apply
```

Resolve checks the official successful native main CI at that revision, actual
archived authorized batch/main PR, exact task set and per-task Merged receipts.
No matching authorized batch is ineligible; a retained/unfinished Coordinator
handoff returns temporary exit 75 so a project can use bounded retries or an
explicit resume. A pending release does not need another owner approval.

The exact configured trusted native verification workflow/job must finish
successfully and its real job log must contain one
`TRACKER_DELIVERY_RECEIPT <compact JSON>` matching the supplied passed
`delivery-verification`: exact configured target, sole admitted merge SHA,
actual acceptance checks and durable report. The project emits that line only
after its real installation/deploy/runtime acceptance. An uploaded arbitrary
manifest is not native success. The recorder re-resolves authorization/tasks,
checks exact official producer/job/revision/log content and persists through
CAS. Same-proof retries are idempotent; cancelled requests, wrong producers,
other revisions/targets, incomplete task handoffs, changed policy and replacing
existing verified proof fail closed. It uses no private-engine access secret.
Partial native reruns may reuse a successful verifier from an earlier actual
attempt when only downstream receipt recording reruns. The recorder inspects
native attempt membership and requires the latest actual configured verifier;
any newer verifier supersedes older proof, including failed, skipped or running
verification. Projects retain request/evidence artifacts from their real producer
attempts instead of deriving their names from the latest overall run attempt.

See [TT-127](https://github.com/MojoTheApe/task-tracker/issues/127) and its
Master companion [MR-28](https://github.com/MojoTheApe/master-repo/issues/28).

### Owner-approved historical completion

An adoption may preserve an explicitly audited set of completed tasks instead of
inventing old delivery receipts. This is optional and never enabled by an engine
upgrade. With the owner's recorded approval, use the candidate config and original
pre-delivery config to propose a manifest:

```sh
python -m tracker --config candidate/tracker/config.json audit-history \
  --legacy-config original/tracker/config.json --source-revision ORIGINAL_FULL_SHA \
  --approved-by "Owner decision in adoption issue" --report "Durable audit reference"
```

This reads current Issues and writes nothing. Review its complete task list and
place only `historical_completion` in the candidate project config and matching
registry fallback config. Commit through the adoption PR. The manifest records
repository, exact target policy, original config hash/revision, audit date, owner
approval reference, report and each task's public ID and accepted-scope hash.
Attestations are reviewed records, not cryptographic proof of owner identity.
Never regenerate or extend the list automatically at cutover or an engine upgrade;
report changed tasks and obtain a new explicit reconciliation decision if needed.

Only original completed, unblocked, unarchived tasks qualify. A new/incomplete
task, changed body/title/identity/state or changed functional/workflow labels cannot
borrow that acceptance. Release membership, priority, milestone and comments do
not change accepted scope; normal release rollover therefore preserves history.
Restarting a listed task through `work` permanently supersedes historical acceptance
before the status write. Direct GitHub changes are compared with the audited state;
the snapshot reader cannot detect an unobserved edit that was fully reverted.
Use a follow-up ticket for new work, or `work` after explicitly reopening with its
new scope. Any delivery record, including failed/revoked/old-policy records,
supersedes the historical exception.

The UI badge says **Done · Accepted before adoption** for accepted historical
Merged tasks that are still complete. Their always-visible task details say
**Completed before adoption** and explain the absence of current-policy delivery
verification. **Delivered** is reserved for actual verified delivery. This is a
completion display label;
the underlying state stays `historical`, distinct from `verified`, with no new
receipt. Such tasks count in completion and dependencies,
but produce no review, stage, merge or installation evidence. Admission commands
do not consult this exception. Release publication still requires the explicit
`--published` confirmation and all existing scope, metadata and dependency checks.
Unlisted work follows every new requirement. A policy change invalidates the
manifest and requires explicit reconciliation; it is not silently grandfathered.

## Optional instruction-only process route

The separate top-level `process_instructions` setting is mirrored exactly as
`delivery.json.workflow.process_instructions`. It requires the independent-review
delivery policy and never changes its fingerprint or inherits on export. Read
[PROCESS_INSTRUCTIONS.md](PROCESS_INSTRUCTIONS.md) for the fixed eligible paths,
complete Git proof, actual process check names, independent ownership and exact
merged evidence. Eligible one-task sources target main and complete from their
verified process merge receipt; ordinary changes keep this document’s delivery
flow. Legacy uses its actual task slot and review attestation; execution-v1/v2/v3
uses the real source review lane. V2 process sources cannot become Approved or
enter intake/batches. A process lane blocks new intake/batch claims, and held
stage/intake/integration blocks process acquisition. Idle stage gaps can bridge
only current retained verified process merges under the pinned proof, with full
normal checks/review/stage verification and unchanged frozen main afterward.


## Explicit post-main application acceptance recovery

An admitted application batch can retain its integration lane after main while
its original acceptance checkboxes remain unchecked. Editing those checkboxes
changes frozen scope. Instead, the actual retained independent integration
Reviewer may use `record-acceptance --pr MAIN_PR --actor Reviewer-ID --session
ACTUAL_SESSION --claim RETAINED_LANE --evidence-file acceptance.json` (preview;
add `--apply` to journal). This does not edit an Issue, finish a task, change a
policy or publish a package. The Coordinator and member implementers cannot
attest their own acceptance. Do not use it for partially implemented outcomes.

The document has `kind: post-main-acceptance`, a concrete `report`, exact
`batch_id`, promotion `pr`, actual `merge_sha`, `head_sha`, combined `tree_sha`,
`policy`, frozen ordered `issues` and `source_heads`, original `issue_scopes`
keyed by decimal Issue number, retained `reviewer`, `review_session`,
`execution_lane`, `coordinator` and `coordinator_session`. `criteria` is keyed
by exactly the members with unchecked work. Each value lists every unchecked
line in original order, including its one-based `line`, literal `criterion`,
`result: passed` and concrete nonempty `evidence`. Fenced examples are excluded.
The receipt validates the admitted promotion, source inclusion, original review,
passed stage/tree and required checks. It cannot waive any of them.

After recording, use ordinary `merged ... --pr MAIN_PR` preview and then
`--apply --reviewed-complete`. Completion rechecks the current receipt and task
scope before all writes and each task write; uncertain writes retain normal
ownership and resume behavior. The same evidence is retained for idempotent
completion and exact-source cleanup. Missing/partial/stale evidence fails closed.
Original task bodies, approvals and reviews remain unchanged. Parent/sibling
outcomes outside the frozen batch remain unfinished. Public snapshots exclude
acceptance reports, sessions and private ownership.

For an already admitted batch blocked on an older consumer pin, use a clean,
independently reviewed fixed-engine checkout with the exact original consumer
config: `python -m tracker --config /absolute/original/tracker/config.json
record-acceptance ...`, then normal `merged` commands. Do not patch cached
runtime code, change config or adopt a new policy. This explicit engine invocation
is recovery only; permanent consumer-pin adoption is separately tracked/reviewed.

# Explicit historical package delivery reconciliation

`legacy-delivery` is a bounded recovery operator for original minimal pre-batch
pending receipts retained by a genuine inspected staging-only policy migration.
It is not ordinary admission, a batch producer, a release command or an extension
of `historical_completion`. Missing receipts, modern batches, failed/verified
records and incomplete business acceptance cannot use it.

Use a clean independently reviewed **merged** engine with the consumer's exact
current `tracker/config.json`. The existing compatible consumer pin and snapshot
writer need no change; never patch a runtime cache, deploy the service or upgrade
another project as a test. First prepare and independently review the complete
allowlist and factual audit, then inspect a zero-write preview:

```sh
python -m tracker --config /absolute/project/tracker/config.json legacy-delivery \
  --evidence-file /private/audited-legacy-delivery.json
# After inspecting the unchanged exact manifest and preview:
python -m tracker --config /absolute/project/tracker/config.json legacy-delivery \
  --evidence-file /private/audited-legacy-delivery.json --apply
```

The manifest has these fields. Hashes are lower-case SHA-256; `digest` below is
`tracker.delivery_receipt.digest` (canonical compact sorted JSON). Issue numbers
are GitHub Issue numbers in this repository, not guessed public task IDs.

| Field | Required evidence |
| --- | --- |
| `kind`, `schema_version` | `legacy-delivery-reconciliation`, integer `1` |
| `repository`, `policy`, `config_sha256` | Exact current official repository, `delivery_policy.fingerprint(config)`, `digest(config)` of the entire loaded current config |
| `issues` | Explicit unique ordered selected Issue numbers, 1–128 |
| `authorization` | New actual owner decision: `approved_by`, concrete `report`, exact same ordered `issues`; previous migration retention is never permission |
| `implementer`, `report` | Actual implementation identity and durable complete-scope audit reference |
| `tasks` | Exactly the selected decimal Issue keys, each with the per-task attestation below |
| `migration_sha256` | `digest` of the genuine unchanged `delivery_workflow.policy_migrations` audit that retained the selected original records |
| `native` | Original unchanged `request` and exact `receipt`, actual integer `run`/`job`, full actual installed-package `report` object |
| `release` | Exact published release `id`, and exactly three `assets`: installer, `release.json`, `release.json.sig`; each includes `id`, `name`, `size`, `digest` from official GitHub metadata |

Each `tasks["NUMBER"]` contains `id` (actual public task ID), `scope`
(`delivery_policy.task_scope(issue)`), `accepted_scope`
(`delivery_policy.accepted_scope_digest(issue)`), `receipt_sha256`
(`delivery_policy.receipt_digest(original_pending_receipt)`), actual independent
`reviewer` distinct from `implementer`, `verdict: complete`, concrete durable
`report` and nonempty `checks` listing passed full-scope evidence. Review the full
original task, branches, source PRs, follow-ups, acceptance and live-business
requirements. A package smoke test alone does not establish business completion.
Attestations are reviewed records, not cryptographic proof of identity. Keep
private evidence and any sensitive details out of public PRs/logs.

The operator requires unchanged Merged scope/identity, no unfinished checklist
(outside fenced examples), no blocker/archive and no selected active ownership.
A successful minimal `{title, state: created, issue}` Issue-creation journal from
`work` remains unchanged as creation history; it is not active ownership. Pending,
uncertain or claimed selected intake still blocks.
Root `todo_order` retains manual sort positions: `queue.ordered_todo` first
filters actual Todo labels. A selected exact Merged task's leftover position is
not ownership; preserve the complete list without editing or dropping entries.
Actual live Todo/multiple statuses, claims, review/approval queues and running
batch/intake/run ownership remain blocked. Malformed sort metadata fails closed.

Normal `catalog.restore` removes the Issue archive flag but retains the completed
execution archive journal. Only the exact empty `implementers`/`state: archived`
stub can be treated as non-owning history here, and only with its genuine archive
history and complete official archive-label then later removal events bracketing
the recorded archive time. Current accepted Merged scope must remain unarchived;
extra author/claim/batch fields, `archiving`, missing/stale restoration proof or a
new current archive cannot use this exception. The stub/history are never edited.
The concrete ACL-1313 case is substantiated by official events
[33307225956](https://api.github.com/repos/MojoTheApe/adopy-campaing-launcher/issues/events/33307225956)
and
[33307524304](https://api.github.com/repos/MojoTheApe/adopy-campaing-launcher/issues/events/33307524304).

It reconstructs each original official historical stage-to-main source linkage,
merge SHA/tree and ancestry to both current main and the actual installed source.
The immutable previous official config must substantiate the original fingerprint
and inspected staging-only audit. It never invents modern source reviews or
admits historical PRs as new frozen batches.

Package evidence is independently corroborated, not accepted from uploaded JSON
or a green generic CI. Native log transport privately captures the bounded output
and retries with gh’s escape opt-in only on its explicit compatibility rejection.
The original archived delivery request, exact task set,
authorization digest, official main batch/merge/tree and successful main CI stay
unchanged. Its trusted native workflow/job and latest actual verifier must match
the exact successful native receipt in the real job log. The complete installed
report must also occur exactly once as actual native stdout. The report binds
passed Windows install/update/restart/recovery/data checks, valid publisher
signature/key identity, source/tree and signed manifest/installer hashes. Official
stable release and asset IDs, sizes and hashes must still match. GitHub releases
need not enable their optional immutable flag: exact native content hashes and
asset identities prevent a mutable tag/asset replacement from borrowing proof.
A download counter change is not a source/content change.

The original producer's task scope is preserved. For example, an original request
for one task remains that one task even when its real package acceptance supports
an explicitly authorized **new** retrospective record for audited older tasks.
The operator never edits that request or claims those older tasks ran in its batch.

Preview performs no writes. Apply makes a single supported compare-and-swap write
changing only selected normal `delivery_workflow.tasks` rows to current-policy
verified delivery, preserving each exact minimal original in `history`. A private
additive audit retains the new owner decision, scope/reviewer, manifest digest,
original producer reference/content digests and release identities. Existing
compatible e775 readers project these ordinary verified receipts unchanged;
portable exports, admission, state protocol and historical exemptions do not change.
Unselected receipts, claims, owners, queues and original native requests stay exact.

Unrelated Workers, Reviewers and maintenance can remain active; this receipt-only
operation does not reserve global maintenance or require global idleness. A newer
state write causes CAS rejection; inspect a fresh preview and retry instead of
replaying a stale state body. Current Issues, main/config and release identities
are re-read before the write. The actual native run/current attempts/latest
verifier and exact receipt/report stdout are also re-read through uncached
transport immediately before CAS: a superseding failed, running or different
verifier cannot borrow the original success even when Tracker state is unchanged.
Inspected same-manifest retries revalidate all proof
and preserve an already-recorded result; different or stale evidence cannot
replace verified delivery. After apply, re-read the stored rows and fresh Tracker
snapshot. A synchronization failure remains unfinished verification.

Master Repo impact: no matching source change. This explicitly invoked operator
uses existing policy, ordinary receipt history and CAS storage without changing
any descriptor/config schema, policy fingerprint, exported helper, admission
rule or public projection. Permanent pin adoption and service publication remain
separate reviewed work.

# Owned maintenance and trusted CI evidence — TT-107

This engine supplies optional support for the reviewed Master requirements in
[MR-26](https://github.com/MojoTheApe/master-repo/issues/26). Installing it changes
no consumer policy, task ownership, state or service. ACL and React Forge retain
their existing pins/configuration and product collectors. Publish compatible
admission writers and the single snapshot writer before reserving a maintenance
interval. Ordinary legacy and execution schemas 1/2/3 keep their adopted behavior.

## Maintenance intervals

`maintenance show` reads private ownership, history, actual readiness and current
state SHA. `maintenance reserve --actor Maintainer-AB12 --session ACTUAL_RUN
--report-file PRIVATE_REPORT [--apply]` previews or reserves one interval through
the same file/SHA compare-and-swap as task admission. The report records actual
authorization and compatible-writer/publication evidence; it contains no secrets.
Persist the returned private claim and reuse it with `--claim` on retries. If the
response is lost after commit, inspect `show` and recover the actual matching
owner. Never manufacture a replacement identity or infer that an owner stopped.

Reservation changes the outer state protocol to 3 and retains the original format
as `maintenance.base_schema_version` (1 or 2). Older engines reject this outer
protocol. A writer that read before reservation loses its stale CAS; after resume,
private history still changes the file SHA, preventing an ABA stale write. New
Workers, source Reviewers, intake/batch owners and integration Reviewers wait.
Existing actual owners retain resume, stopped-owner transfer, handoff, approval,
return, cancellation, stage/main completion and other supported drain operations.
A new repair claim is still new admission; resume the gate explicitly if required.

Reservation is separate from readiness. Active claims/reviews/intakes/batches,
creating-Issue journals, pending author-return/archive journals, release rollover
and unpromoted stage make the interval draining. Queued/Approved sources remain
unfinished but do not themselves own an active lane. The normal migration guards
still validate preserved queues, approvals, exact scope/base/policy and history.
`execution migrate --apply` under a held gate additionally requires its actual
Maintainer `--actor`, `--session`, `--claim`; migration retains the gate. It does
not discard owners, fix approvals, reset stage or complete tasks.

`maintenance resume` with the actual owner/claim/report restores only admission
and the retained underlying state format, adding audit history. Committed resume
and transfer retries are idempotent; an old claim cannot release a later interval.
`maintenance transfer --previous-claim ACTUAL_CLAIM --stopped --actor
Maintainer-CD34 --session ACTUAL_REPLACEMENT --report-file PRIVATE_REPORT --apply`
requires verified stopped execution and a distinct actual replacement. It leaves
all task/reviewer/Coordinator ownership untouched. Preview never persists a claim.

Only a held interval adds public `maintenance`: `admission_paused`, static
`state` (`draining` or `idle`), and a validated UTC `reserved_at`. Claims, actors,
sessions, reports and audit history stay private. Never-held and resumed projects
retain their previous public payloads and digests, including the ACL root bridge.

## Explicit CI evidence policy

`ci_evidence_policy` is optional; export does not inherit it. Schema 1 has exactly
`schema_version: 1` and a nonempty `profiles` map. Adoption must be committed to
actual current-main `tracker/config.json`; source-local or temporary configuration
cannot establish trust. Master owns any descriptor mirror/consumer adoption.
Existing configured required checks, independent review, actual stage/delivery
freshness and manual/release policy remain authoritative. Coverage is advisory;
consumer-owned CI runs every reported missing job and keeps its required aggregate
successful only after covered plus fresh jobs actually pass.

Each profile has `workflow_path`, immutable Git `workflow_blob_sha`,
`producer_files` (repository paths to immutable Git blob SHAs), `jobs`,
`max_age_seconds` (explicit 1..2592000 lifetime from actual job completion), and
`metadata_mode` (`commit` by default when authoring; `tree` requires explicit
review). Protocol validation requires the field to be explicit. Commit mode
requires the actual tested commit, including Git metadata. Tree mode requires the
entire tested tree to equal the actual candidate; it must only be adopted when
commit/branch/history-sensitive behavior is excluded by review.

A full native job name maps either to `{ "mode": "fresh" }`, for contexts that
cannot be proven, or to a fixed-job definition with exactly:

- `mode: "fixed"`, unique static `workflow_job`, stable exact `runner_labels`;
- `producer_step`, `producer_path`, and ordered nonempty `verification_steps`;
- `context`: digest-pinned `container`, explicit `host_independent: true`, exact
  observed `toolchains` (`python3`, `node`, `npm`, full versions), nonempty
  `dependencies`, and `build_inputs`/`fixtures`, each a path-to-Git-blob map.

The container must contain the reviewed resolved dependencies; lock/build/fixture
blobs bind those inputs independently on the target. Review its immutable build
and verification commands before adoption. Commands that install mutable inputs,
external fixtures, host-dependent behavior, Windows/installer acceptance or an
unproven environment use `fresh`. This is a bounded container/userland protocol,
not a claim to resolve arbitrary environments, runner images or external systems.

V1 deliberately accepts static **JSON-formatted workflows** (an unambiguous YAML
subset). Each fixed native job has the exact profile name, stable runner labels,
digest-pinned container, no matrix/reusable job/inherited env/defaults/conditions,
no self-hosted runner/mutable services/environment, and begins with `actions/checkout@FULL_IMMUTABLE_SHA` with default checkout. The
next step is exactly `{ "name": PRODUCER_STEP, "run": COMMAND }`, where COMMAND
is the shell-quoted sequence:

```sh
python3 -I scripts/tracker_ci_evidence.py emit-context --profile PROFILE --job 'FULL NATIVE JOB NAME'
```

Use the actual adopted producer path. Pin the exported helper's Git blob in
`producer_files`. V1 additionally verifies its bytes are exactly the maintained
self-contained producer at this pinned engine; wrappers/custom import closures
are unsupported and require fresh jobs. Isolated Python (`-I`) excludes repository
sidecars, `PYTHONPATH` and user-site hooks from producer imports. Every
following step is an explicitly named unconditional `run` verification step,
listed in order. Arbitrary annotations, uploaded JSON, cache hits, green aggregate
names and run-level artifact digests never establish producer/context trust.
Unsupported YAML/matrices/reusable workflows require fresh jobs until a separately
reviewed producer protocol supports them; existing product collectors continue.

The trusted producer observes actual Git HEAD/tree and input blobs, actual exact
toolchain versions and native run/attempt/workflow identity before any repository
test or dependency hook runs. It emits one versioned marker. The shipped producer
retains the step for two seconds after flushing the marker because native step
boundaries have second precision; a marker from a later test cannot enter its
proof window. Logs are read privately, never stored or published wholesale.

## Collect and plan coverage

```sh
python -m tracker ci-evidence collect --profile PROFILE --run ACTUAL_RUN --source-pr PR --apply
python -m tracker ci-evidence coverage --profile PROFILE --pr PR --head EXPECTED_HEAD --context source
```

Collection independently verifies the official repository, actual successful
native run and latest attempt, immutable workflow/producer blobs, each actual
native job/check linkage, producer step window and every actual successful test
step. For a PR it verifies the **actual default synthetic checkout** and its
ordered current base/head parents; `run.head_sha` alone is not tested content.
An open ready unchanged official PR is required. Historical/closed PR synthetic
checkout guesses are unsupported. Push/dispatch collection binds their actual
head checkout, but v1 reuse remains tied to the explicit supported PR contexts.
The recorded source binding retains current task scope, branch/base/head and
adopted delivery/execution policy. No file-import command is provided.

The versioned private record retains tested commit/tree, profile/context digest,
actual run/job/attempt/URLs, native job-log provenance and an empty artifact list.
V1 does **not** infer a producing job or attempt from native run-level artifact
metadata, does not reuse packages, and supplies no installer/runtime attestation.
A later package adapter requires actual immutable artifact-to-job proof. CAS
collection conserves all unrelated state, can occur while admission is held, and
recovers an uncertain committed write by its stable proof identity.

Coverage revalidates every retained producer against native GitHub metadata/logs;
a hash-correct uploaded/fabricated stored record cannot become trust. It resolves
target context independently from current-main adoption and actual target Git
blobs. Changed content, workflow/helper, locks/toolchains/inputs or actual attempt
requires fresh proof. Missing/failed/skipped/cancelled/ambiguous jobs are missing,
never inferred from a successful aggregate. Covered output names actual run/job
IDs, attempt and producer URL; union retains those real producer references and
still reports every missing platform/job.

For `--context integration`, the actual frozen integration batch, unchanged open
Approved source PRs, current retained independent approvals/scope/base/policy,
ordered membership and native merge composition are revalidated. Source evidence
can cover only the **entire identical combined candidate tree**; different source
trees cannot be unioned to prove a changed batch. One member still requires normal
independent combined review. Manual, release, promotion and runtime contexts
report all jobs missing and preserve their existing full/fresh product gates.
No coverage result replaces `check-pr`, `check-merge`, actual review or delivery.

# Parallel execution contract v1

This document describes execution policy schema 1. Schemas 2/3 use
[Approved tasks and frozen integration batches](BATCH_INTEGRATION.md), sharing the
Worker claim/handoff and independent identity rules but releasing source review
at Approved and reserving integration separately. Installing a newer engine does
not switch modes.

Two workers can implement independent tasks in separate agent runs, branches and
worktrees. One reviewer processes ready tasks sequentially and keeps the same lane
through review, fixes, stage (where configured), checks and main integration.
Waiting in Review does not consume an implementation slot. A dependent task waits
for its dependency's configured completion, including delivery when required.

This is explicit per-project adoption. Neither a shared engine upgrade nor a new
installed skill enables it. `tracker/config.json` accepts:

```json
"execution_policy": {"schema_version": 1, "implementation_limit": 2, "review_limit": 1}
```

It requires the existing [delivery policy](DELIVERY_POLICY.md). Master Repo mirrors
the same object in `delivery.json` at `workflow.execution`. Limits are repository
wide across all cooperating platforms/sessions. Implementation capacity accepts
1–16; review capacity is exactly 1. Capacity changes require an idle migration,
not rewriting the live claims. One source PR contains one task in this version.
Research/operations can use a PR containing their report; `complete` cannot bypass
the independent review lane. Legacy projects retain their existing commands.

## Adoption order

1. Finish the adoption PR under the old rules. Inventory active Issues, branches,
   claims, pending batches, reviews and stage work. Preserve completion evidence:
   execution-only adoption/capacity changes leave delivery receipts and historical
   manifests valid. Changes to the actual delivery policy still require its
   existing explicit evidence reconciliation.
2. Update all writers, generated PR helpers, exact engine pins and the snapshot
   service to a compatible reviewed revision. Deploying that service is a separate
   maintained release step; merging this source does not update the live website.
   Preserve the old config and a private copy of shared state for recovery.
3. Commit the matching opt-in config through the project's authorized adoption.
   Preview `execution migrate`, then `execution migrate --apply`. It refuses live
   In Progress/Review/Stage tasks, legacy claims/running batches and active stage.
   It preserves history and delivery data while using state schema 2. Preview makes
   no writes; repeating an already applied migration is safe.
4. Verify a fresh board snapshot and use only the pinned compatible client. Older
   state-aware clients reject schema 2. Do not resume older writers or remove the
   policy as a rollback: reconcile all work while idle before restoring anything.

## Roles and claims

The coordinator uses neutral names such as `Coordinator-A7F2`, `Worker-B3K8` and
`Reviewer-C9M4` (role plus 4–32 alphanumeric characters). Generate a distinct opaque
session ID for each actual agent run, retain it on resume, and never rename a run
to claim independence. A session can register only one worker/reviewer actor.
GitHub Assignee remains a real account and is never overwritten with these names.
The web drawer displays coordinator, worker, reviewer and work state separately.

The tracker reserves work; the coordinator uses the host's actual delegation
capabilities. It does not spawn a model or open chats. Start at most the configured
number of workers and launch an independent reviewer when a task is ready and the
review lane is free. Workers do not independently launch reviewers. If independent
agent runs are unavailable, explain the serial implementation fallback and obtain
a real independent reviewer through available project tooling. Never fabricate one.

Use `python scripts/task_tracker.py` in a consumer, or `python -m tracker` in the
engine checkout. Read the current task and applicable instructions before each
claim. The following identity/path values are illustrative:

```sh
python scripts/task_tracker.py start EX-12 \
  --actor Worker-B3K8 --session run_b3k8 --coordinator Coordinator-A7F2 \
  --branch work/ex-12-search --worktree /worktrees/ex-12
```

`work` accepts the same flags for immediate existing/new requests. `start` returns
a private `claim.id`; reserve before the worker edits code. Give each worker only
its task, worktree, ID and necessary context. The second claim repeats this with a
different task/run/branch/worktree. A third claim waits when both slots are full.
Do not use the legacy `queue begin/next/release/cancel` operations in this mode;
claim the owner's explicitly selected tasks individually.

`execution show` is a private diagnostic containing paths, claims and reports.
It must not be published. Actor IDs are attestations by cooperating agents, not
new authentication principals. GitHub permissions and merge protections remain
authoritative; direct GitHub writes or forged sessions are not prevented by these
records. No credentials or secrets belong in shared state or reports.

## Handoff, review and integration

Push a ready source PR with the exact task link and existing naming/check rules.
For execution-enabled projects, `work/<ticket-id>-<short-name>` and the existing
`codex/` prefix are accepted; retain an explicit host/user branch requirement.
Write the actual scope, checks/results, PR, base and remaining risks in a handoff
file and keep the Issue Specifications current. Then:

```sh
python scripts/task_tracker.py execution handoff EX-12 --pr 45 \
  --actor Worker-B3K8 --session run_b3k8 --claim CLAIM_ID --report-file handoff.md
python scripts/task_tracker.py execution review-acquire --pr 45 \
  --actor Reviewer-C9M4 --session review_c9m4 --coordinator Coordinator-A7F2
```

Handoff journals before changing the label, verifies Review, then releases only
that implementation claim and enqueues the task. The one review reservation is
atomic across sessions; it rejects every recorded implementer session, including
previous owners. The coordinator chooses a ready task (normally oldest first);
queue order is visible but strict FIFO is not required. Save the returned review
`id`. `record-review` evidence keeps the existing exact head/base/tree/report and
recorded `implementer`, plus the lane owner's `reviewer`, `review_session` and
`execution_lane`. It rejects stale or foreign evidence. Resume an existing lane
with `review-acquire` and its `--claim`, actor/session and PR.

Run normal `check-pr`, independent review, required checks, `record-review` and
`check-merge` immediately before merging. Stage-enabled projects still use working
branch → stage → main, exact content verification and the existing one-candidate
rule. The reviewer finishes the entire lane before taking another task. After a
verified main merge, run `merged ID --pr MAIN_PR` dry run, then
`--apply --reviewed-complete`. Only after receipts and labels succeed is the lane
released. Production/package verification remains a separate existing requirement;
the lane does not publish, install or falsely claim delivery. Before the next
task's approval, update against the new main and repeat affected checks/review.

## Failures, fixes and stopped agents

- Uncertain writes keep the claim. Inspect `execution show` and Issues, then
  repeat the same operation. For an uncertain start, use `start --resume` with the
  original flags and `--claim`. For an uncertain handoff, repeat its exact PR/report
  and claim. Do not infer success, free capacity or abandonment from elapsed time.
- A worker that cannot proceed uses `execution stop ID --actor ... --session ...
  --claim ... --report-file ...`. It journals the handoff, moves the task to blocked
  Todo and releases its claim. Resolve the report before unblocking/reclaiming it.
- If a worker has actually stopped, the coordinator can use `execution takeover
  ID --previous-claim OLD --stopped --reason ...` with new worker/session and
  explicit branch/worktree/coordinator fields. Inspect/reuse the prior work. This
  rotates ownership and records both implementers; old claims cannot resume,
  stop or hand off. Pending handoff/stop writes must be reconciled first.
- The reviewer requests fixes with `execution review-return --actor ... --session
  ... --claim LANE_ID --report-file ...`. Before a source merge this frees the lane
  and returns the task to Todo. The author takes a fresh implementation claim.
  Add `--keep-lane` to retain integration ownership; this is mandatory after the
  source has entered stage. The worker still consumes an implementation slot while
  fixing it and hands off a ready source PR from the same working branch. That
  handoff resumes the same reviewer and invalidated proof must be repeated.
- If the reviewer stops, use `execution review-takeover --previous-claim OLD
  --stopped --reason ...` with a new independent reviewer/session/coordinator. It
  preserves the occupied lane, rotates the claim and invalidates approval. A
  replacement can review the actual merged source in stage or main with `record-review`;
  unchanged exact-content stage verification remains subject to normal gates.

Reservations use GitHub contents SHA compare-and-swap. Label changes are separate
GitHub writes, so recovery deliberately retains ownership until verification.
Stopping the previous process before takeover is essential: a claim is not a
remote process kill switch. Never force-clear another lane or hand-edit shared
state to bypass a failed check.

## Compatibility and publication

`export-template --execution-policy FILE` exports the explicit policy alongside
`--delivery-policy FILE`; absence strips any engine-owned execution setting.
Schema-1 projects and snapshots remain supported. Schema-2 public snapshots expose
capacity, neutral roles and review position, but omit session/claim IDs, filesystem
paths, reports and actor history. The UI is still read-only.

Tracked by [TT-67](https://github.com/MojoTheApe/task-tracker/issues/67) and companion
[MR-11](https://github.com/MojoTheApe/master-repo/issues/11). This change enables
adoption; it does not migrate ACL or any other existing project.

## Optional instruction-only process route

The separate top-level `process_instructions` setting is mirrored exactly as
`delivery.json.workflow.process_instructions`. It requires the independent-review
delivery policy and never changes its fingerprint or inherits on export. Read
[PROCESS_INSTRUCTIONS.md](PROCESS_INSTRUCTIONS.md) for the fixed eligible paths,
complete Git proof, actual process check names, independent ownership and exact
merged evidence. Eligible one-task sources target main and complete from their
verified process merge receipt; ordinary changes keep this document’s delivery
flow. Legacy uses its actual task slot and review attestation; execution-v1/v2
uses the real source review lane. V2 process sources cannot become Approved or
enter intake/batches. A process lane blocks new intake/batch claims, and held
stage/intake/integration blocks process acquisition. Idle stage gaps can bridge
only current retained verified process merges under the pinned proof, with full
normal checks/review/stage verification and unchanged frozen main afterward.

# Reviewed repository instructions

This optional route lets a complete instruction-only source PR merge to main
without a stage or package cycle. The task, independent review and successful
configured checks remain required. The repository owner opts in explicitly with
matching `process_instructions` in `tracker/config.json` and
`workflow.process_instructions` in `delivery.json`:

```json
{"schema_version": 1, "required_checks": ["descriptor", "tracker-link", "Process instructions"]}
```

Names identify actual successful GitHub Actions checks on the exact source head.
The list must be unique, nonblank and include `descriptor` and `tracker-link`.
The opt-in requires an existing independent-review delivery policy; a malformed
manual config without one fails validation. Its delivery fingerprint does not change. An absent setting
preserves the existing legacy, execution-v1 or execution-v2/v3 lifecycle. Adoption,
service installation and deployment require their existing explicit authorization.
Export uses `export-template --process-instructions POLICY.json`; the exporter
never inherits this setting from the engine configuration. Master initializer and
validator support are tracked in [MR-16](https://github.com/MojoTheApe/master-repo/issues/16).

## Fixed eligibility

Only root `AGENTS.md`, root `CLAUDE.md`, and Markdown files beneath
`docs/repository/` qualify. A nonempty complete diff is reconstructed from both
immutable Git trees and verified Git blobs. Every changed file must be a normal
non-executable regular UTF-8 file, bounded to one MiB and without binary NULs.
Additions and deletions qualify; a rename qualifies only when both paths qualify.
Symlinks, executable modes, unsafe paths, missing content, malformed or truncated
trees cannot establish this route. Mixed changes, configuration, scripts, CI,
runtime, product and other documentation retain the ordinary delivery route.
Titles, labels, author claims and opt-out text cannot select the exception.

The exact opt-in must already exist in both authoritative base configuration and
base descriptor; a caller's temporary configuration cannot activate it. The
working source includes the exact main baseline. The exported portable helper
`tracker_process_instructions.py` exposes `policy(config)`,
`classify(request, config, pr)` and
`classify_local(config, repository, base_sha, head_sha)`. Classification returns
`None` for empty or mixed diffs, a complete immutable proof for eligible changes,
or raises `ValueError` when proof is unsafe or incomplete. The local classifier
uses the same predicate and complete Git objects. CI separately establishes the
actual repository, event, main/source refs and current revisions.

## Review, merge and recovery

Create and claim the actual task before work. A process source links exactly one
task and targets main using the normal ticket branch/title convention. Legacy
projects retain their existing task slot and distinct independent reviewer and
implementer attestation. Execution-v1/v2/v3 projects use the actual Worker handoff,
Reviewer claim/session and source review lane. In v2/v3 this route goes Review to
Merged: it cannot become Approved, enter an intake/batch or acquire Coordinator
integration ownership. Other tasks continue to use their ordinary flow.

`record-review` binds the independent report to the exact source head, main base,
resulting tree, complete instruction diff, task scope and process policy. Run
`check-merge` immediately before the real merge; it verifies current main, current
scope/dependencies, actual successful checks and current independent ownership.
Held stage, integration or running intake work blocks process review acquisition
and merge until that work finishes. A held process source review lane prevents
new intake or batch claims through the same state CAS, including retained fix
ownership. This prevents silently invalidating frozen work.

After the actual merge, use the normal reviewed `merged` dry run and apply. Its
first parent must equal the reviewed main base, and its tree must equal the
reviewed source tree; merge resolution or extra content invalidates the proof.
The retained process receipt is verified review/merge evidence. It makes the task
complete without pretending that a package was published or a deployment ran.
Public snapshots expose only a safe completion flag; reports, manifests, sessions,
claims and private history stay in durable private state. Dependencies and release
readiness use the same genuine completion receipt.

Concurrent writes fail the normal state CAS. Partial label/completion operations
can resume without losing review or ownership. A stopped execution Reviewer may
be replaced through the existing explicit takeover, with a fresh independent
review of the actual merged source and first parent before completion. Old
completed PRs cannot complete reopened execution tasks or changed task scopes.
After a completed process merge, the next ordinary stage candidate may bridge an
idle stage-to-main instruction gap only when the pinned helper proves the complete
eligible diff and every intervening first-parent merge has its retained current
verified process receipt, independent review, policy and unchanged task scope.
Unknown commits, missing receipts or unsafe changes fail. This read-only allowance
never resets a branch; current main remains the exact frozen candidate baseline.
Ordinary source checks, combined review, full CI, actual stage verification and
unchanged main promotion remain mandatory.

Implementation: [TT-79](https://github.com/MojoTheApe/task-tracker/issues/79).

# Task context and retained source approvals

This shared protocol implements WFO-01 through WFO-04 (TT-136 and Master MR-30).
It applies to every delivery profile through an explicit matching descriptor
`workflow.task_context` and Tracker `task_context_policy`, both exactly
`{"schema_version": 1}`. V1 requires execution schema 2 or 3. Absence preserves
the exact existing lifecycle, whole-body scope hashes and main-bound approval.
No CI reuse, new board status, service deployment or consumer activation follows
from engine support. The optional Stage and actual delivery profiles are unchanged.

## Assessment before development

Read the complete Issue, relevant code/system decisions, related tasks (including
completed work) and dependencies. Determine whether the original result is still
needed and consistent. Do not infer relevance from age, labels or a matching title.
Unchanged authorized work proceeds; a material change to the owner's outcome or
an unresolved authorization boundary needs their decision. The machine validates
binding/completeness, not the truth of a semantic assessment.

Create a planning Issue first when its ID is not known. `work --title` cannot
invent an assessment of a speculative ID: it may leave the created task in
Backlog until assessment is recorded. Before `work ID`/`start ID`, obtain current
identity with:

```sh
python -m tracker task-context assess EX-12 --actor Worker-W001 --session actual_run
```

Copy the returned identity into a JSON document. Add `verdict` (`ready`,
`needs-clarification` or `superseded`) and concrete nonempty `code`, `decisions`,
`related_work`, `dependencies` and `report` strings. Record with the same command
plus `--evidence-file readiness.json --apply`. Negative conclusions remain durable
assessments and grant no start. Start with that same genuine Worker/session.
Changed requirements or main and a new owner require a current assessment; an
unchanged same-owner resume reuses it. Claims/status writes still enforce all
existing classification, dependency, capacity and ownership gates.

## Requirements and the terminal working journal

All Issue text remains authoritative except one explicitly paired terminal block:

```text
<!-- tracker-journal:start -->
### Handoff
Current branch, PR, observations and dated verification history.
<!-- tracker-journal:end -->
```

Markers are exact standalone lines, appear once in that order and close the Issue
apart from whitespace. No checklist items, `needs:` dependencies or `Blocked:`
records belong inside. Ambiguous or unsafe placement fails closed. Ordinary
History/Verification headings have no special meaning. Moving or deleting an
outside requirement changes scope. Checkbox state is not normalized away.
New normalized scope has the opaque `v2:` prefix; old hashes always retain their
whole-body meaning. This avoids rehashing historical receipts or allowing a newly
installed engine to reinterpret old proof. Adding/changing only the permitted
journal does not invalidate new-policy source approval or acceptance criteria.

## Compatibility after a forward main change

An Approved source keeps its original author, head/tree, requirements, source
checks and independent review. A changed main still needs an independent semantic
compatibility assessment. Disjoint file paths alone are insufficient. If code or
conflict resolution is necessary, release compatibility review and use the normal
Coordinator return to the author, checks, handoff and independent source approval.

```sh
python -m tracker task-context review-acquire EX-12 --actor Reviewer-R001 --session actual_review --coordinator Coordinator-C001
python -m tracker task-context review-record EX-12 --actor Reviewer-R001 --session actual_review --claim ACTUAL_CLAIM
```

The first reserves an existing bounded source lane; the second previews the exact
evidence identity. Add `verdict: compatible` and nonempty `main_changes`,
`semantic_dependencies`, `checks` and `report`, then record with
`--evidence-file compatibility.json --apply`. The Reviewer must be a genuine
non-implementing run independent of every task implementer. The original approval
and source report are retained; a separate chained receipt binds their digest,
old/current main, exact scope/head/tree, policy and real review owner. No source
test result is relabeled as a test of new main. Status remains Approved.

A held compatibility lane blocks selection of that source into a batch. Return
or interruption cannot manufacture compatibility. The same owner resumes with
the real claim. `execution review-takeover --previous-claim ... --stopped --reason
...` supports a distinct independent replacement after verifying the old run has
stopped; it grants no verdict. `task-context review-release ID` with the real
Reviewer/session/claim and `--report-file` releases the lane without approval.
After an uncertain committed `review-record`, retry the identical evidence and
owner/claim; inspect changed main/scope before proceeding.

Each frozen batch still has independent combined review, composition verification,
all applicable candidate checks, current main admission and any Stage/production/
package checks. Already-frozen members and divergent main use normal held-batch
or author recovery. Multiple sequential batches can revalidate remaining unchanged
sources without inventing author edits or repeating original source review.

## Activation and compatibility

New project state with this explicit policy is initialized by `execution migrate`.
It uses outer protocol 4, retaining execution state 2. Old writers reject it.
Maintenance can wrap protocol 4 and resume it without dropping the fence.

For an existing project, first integrate matching reviewed descriptor/config and
publish compatible actual writers/projection. Under genuine owned maintenance,
drain active owners/intake/stage, then preview/apply `task-context adopt` using the
actual Maintainer actor/session/claim/report. It verifies official current-main
config and preserves queues, old approvals, delivery receipts and history without
rehashing them. Old full-body evidence stays conservative; later newly reviewed
scope uses the explicit journal protocol. Resume the same maintenance owner and
verify the fresh board. No live adoption is part of this source implementation.

# Repository workflow

Read `delivery.json`, the [system description](../system/PROJECT.md),
[delivery rules](DELIVERY.md), [selected Tracker guide](TRACKER.md) and
[verification](VERIFICATION.md) before work. These checked-in files describe this
project's actual immutable standard/engine pair, selected route and local controls.
Use `python scripts/task_tracker.py guide` for the same pinned command guidance.

## Selected route

This project selects execution schema 3 with 5 implementation slots, 5 separately owned source-review slots and one separate integration Reviewer, plus a Coordinator batch reservation. Each ordinary source PR contains exactly one task. Independent source review and checks move it from Review to Approved and release its source-review ownership. Development alone ends at Approved. An integration request selects one frozen batch of 1..5 tasks; no minimum batch size is required. Its separate Coordinator claim preserves every source, author, accepted scope and current approval. Independently review and check the combined candidate; integration/promotion preserves the complete frozen member set and batch identity. Ship-all snapshots current Approved intake, leaving later arrivals for another intake. Stage is disabled: the reserved independently reviewed batch is admitted to main using the pinned batch direction; ordinary sources remain approval-only.



## Adopted instruction-only exception

Use the exact [local process guide](PROCESS_INSTRUCTIONS.md) and its complete immutable-diff classifier. Only proven eligible regular instructions retain genuine author/review ownership and instruction checks through Review -> main -> Merged. Do not move that source to Approved, batch or Stage or manufacture installation proof. Wait for reserved integration/unpromoted Stage ownership. Mixed, unsafe, unknown or incomplete proof follows the selected ordinary route and actual target obligations.

## Work and independent review

Create a real Issue before implementation. Ideas remain Idea; requested tasks
start Backlog. Planning does not claim code capacity. When development is
requested, read the entire Description and Specifications and use the pinned
Tracker's `work` command to claim the actual available slot and verify In Progress.
Follow its supported branch/actor/session rules and any host-required prefix.
An older task needs current readiness assessment, not routine owner reapproval.

The Coordinator checks dependencies, overlap and actual ownership, and delegates
independent eligible work to Workers in isolated branches/worktrees through
available subagents. Respect the selected capacity and any tighter commissioned
work limit. Keep roles separate from GitHub assignees and use genuine opaque
actor/session identities. Do not create new user-owned chats without an explicit
request. If delegation is unavailable, record serial implementation; independent
review still cannot be replaced by self-review.

Prepare a linked PR after implementation and self-checks. Preserve the exact
machine-readable `Tracker issues:` field and source-versus-integration identity
from this project's PR template. No automatic Issue-closing keywords. Update
current system knowledge and meaningful history in the same PR, or explain the
specific no-impact result. Preserve original specifications and local safeguards.

Follow the selected Tracker guide for the genuine handoff and review ownership.
Arrange a separate non-implementing subagent to review the actual head/base, full
requirements, changed files and checks. Delegated Workers hand off to their
Coordinator, who starts the independent review. Keep fixes on the task branch;
reclaim author ownership through the adopted return procedure before editing after
handoff, including base updates or conflict resolution. Reviewers and coordinators
must not edit an unclaimed branch. Changed code, base, scope or policy requires
fresh appropriate proof. A missing independent reviewer is an explicit limitation,
never self-approval.

Use `check-pr` for early linkage feedback and the supported `check-merge` once for
final admission; final admission already includes linkage. Verify actual branch
protection and required checks rather than inferring them from a label or guide.
Preserve exact reviewed content through admitted integration. Use the selected
Tracker guide for evidence, return/takeover, recovery and optional Stage commands;
no timeout or status-label edit clears a genuine owner.

## Local knowledge and delivery

A selected integration/main-merge request includes the maintained delivery and
verification required by this project's adopted target. Continue through
[delivery continuation](DELIVERY_CONTINUATION.md) without a routine second approval;
read [runtime procedures](../runtime/DELIVERY.md) for actual authorization, access,
backup and compatible recovery. Instructions do not create a background producer.
A partial ticket, pending/failed delivery or unknown accepted outcome stays
unfinished. Merge, publication, installation and verified behavior are separate
facts. Do not reduce a completion obligation to bypass missing proof.

Use the [ownership map](LAYOUT.md) for repository/system/runtime files. Shared
upgrades preserve project-owned system/runtime knowledge, unique commands,
installers, data and deployment controls. Ordinary feature work does not upgrade
standard or engine pins. For process changes assess Master Repo / Task Tracker
impact and link the matching fix or concrete no-impact result.

The installed `project-workflow` skill is navigation. Its canonical Master source
and verified AI Skills mirror do not activate this project's policies or replace
its adopted local instructions. Record actual exceptions in `delivery.json`.

Follow the [shared continuation contract](https://github.com/MojoTheApe/master-repo/blob/864ca7a5814e703dd6e61207362d24cbc26dc9ad/docs/delivery-continuation.md)
at this project's exact standard pin and [runtime procedure](../runtime/DELIVERY.md).
Under this adopted flow, owner approval to integrate/merge selected tasks into
main covers review/checks,
optional stage, admitted main merge, maintained delivery, verification and final
Tracker receipt. The owner need not also say “and deliver”. Starting development
or source approval alone does not authorize integration/deployment.
Do not request another routine owner approval after main; report a concrete missing
permission, access or failed check instead.

The Coordinator must continue or hand off durably to the configured project CI.
Shared templates do not create a release/deploy mechanism or a background agent.
For compatible runtime/package batches, the Coordinator persists this standing
authorization by default with `batch begin --deliver --delivery-workflow PATH --delivery-job
EXACT_NAME`, selecting the real project native verification producer. This is an
agent implementation detail, not another approval. Honor explicit source-only or
merge-only/skip-release instructions; deferred runtime delivery stays unfinished.
Use the maintained separate release path when later authorized rather than adding
permission by resuming an old batch. Arbitrary main pushes cannot authorize release. A trusted
workflow can use the exported `tracker_delivery_receipt.py resolve`/`record` with
a same-repository token, successful main CI, actual Merged handoff and exact native
verification job/log proof. Follow the pinned guide; the portable recorder creates
no authorization or deployment. No private engine access token is required.

Before claiming it works automatically, implement and test the project's actual
adapter, including a failed run, resumable retry and duplicate request.

Persist exact merged revision/tree, task set, configured target and run/artifact
identity; serialize changes per target and prevent stale runs replacing newer work.
Verify actual profile-specific acceptance, then record delivery through the exact
pinned Tracker and read back completion. Preserve failed/pending tasks and evidence.
A receipt retry must not repeat a completed install/deploy or create a new version.

Tooling/local and explicitly n8n-source work retains admitted reviewed-merge
completion. Package requires stable publication and agreed installation verification;
VPS/ordinary n8n requires actual configured production behavior. Preserve local
release, credential, backup, rollback and separate authorization controls.

# File ownership

Paths in this document are relative to the repository root.

| Area | Contents | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| `docs/repository/` | Git, tasks, review, checks, adoption and repository change history | Shared process, with reviewed project exceptions |
| `docs/system/` | What the product does, architecture, requirements, domain constraints and system history | Project |
| `docs/runtime/` | Environment identities, credentials handling, operational authorization, deployment, backup and recovery | Project |
| `.workflow/tools/` | Shared exported Tracker helpers | Pinned shared template |
| Application directories | Workflows, generators, tests and product scripts | Project |

`AGENTS.md` is a short reading map. Keep substantive rules in the appropriate
area. Business rules belong to the system, even when an agent must follow them.
A new Git rule belongs to repository guidance. An instruction to access, publish
or test a live environment belongs to runtime guidance. Link between the areas
instead of copying their rules into each other. Mixed legacy documents must be
split by section, preserving their requirements and dated evidence.

`delivery.json` and `tracker/config.json` are the small machine-readable bridge:
they identify checks and completion policy and may link project procedures. They
are not places for a product specification or full operational runbook.

New projects receive starting outlines in `docs/system/` and `docs/runtime/`.
Those files become project-owned immediately, even before they are customized.
Standard upgrades never replace, merge or delete their contents. Missing required
project documents need explicit repair in a project PR. The recorded template
baseline stays pristine; it is not a backup or authority for project knowledge.

Upgrades of an earlier mixed layout stop without writes for an audited migration.
Move the original material, adjust links, preserve local safeguards and record the
move map. Old paths may remain short forwarding files; do not maintain two copies
of the rules. Existing `scripts/task_tracker.py` and related helper paths are
compatibility entry points only; implementations live in `.workflow/tools/`.

This layout alone changes no task status, delivery policy or deployment connection.
The separately adopted `process_instructions` option selects an instruction-only
integration route; follow the pinned workflow and actual diff classification.

# Project delivery

`delivery.json` records this project's intent; `tracker/config.json` is the
matching executable selection. Both use exact compatible immutable pins. Source
configuration, an installed engine or navigation skill never activates a new
state contract. Populate actual procedures and retain verified registry/live-board
proof before changing adoption from draft to ready.

## Selected integration and target

This package project remains unfinished after main until the maintained producer publishes the stable release and verifies installation for the exact accepted source/task/target. Record the genuine delivery receipt; merge or a tag alone is insufficient. Stage is explicitly disabled and does not require a Stage receipt. An authorized eligible runtime/package integration uses the pinned batch delivery continuation by default, unless explicitly deferred. Source approval alone authorizes no delivery.



The [selected local Tracker guide](TRACKER.md) owns precise commands, claims,
source-versus-integration membership, evidence and recovery. Preserve its current
scope, policy, source tree and target bindings. A label, closed Issue or source
merge cannot replace required independent review, checks or target verification.
Keep partial tasks and unknown/pending/failed delivery unfinished. Historical
acceptance retains only its exact proven bounds.

## Authorized continuation

A request to integrate selected work into main includes its maintained delivery
and verification; do not add routine reapproval after the merge. Follow
[delivery continuation](DELIVERY_CONTINUATION.md), honoring an explicit source-only
or deferred-release instruction while keeping any resulting runtime obligation
unfinished. Use only the project's actual maintained producer/adapter and local
[operational procedures](../runtime/DELIVERY.md). A guide is not a background
listener or release dispatcher. Never manufacture installation or business proof.

Verify actual native protection separately and keep configured checks current.
Reconcile real scope/conflicts through a claimed author and fresh review. Preserve
original history, current owners, pending operations, backups and compatible
recovery; do not roll back accepted newer state for an incompatible old reader.
Never delete permanent branches or rewrite project data to make a gate pass.

## Onboarding and ownership

Keep local environment identities, access, authorization and data safeguards in
`docs/runtime/DELIVERY.md`; keep product truth in `docs/system/`. Generation and
three-way upgrades preserve both areas and unique project behavior. Record
project exceptions explicitly rather than silently rewriting shared intent.

Onboarding proof identifies the exact workspace project, actual registry
publication, labels/branches and a fresh correct live board with saved links.
A generated directory or local registry change is not a connected project. Keep
setup pending where proof is missing. No credentials or private reports belong
in published project or Tracker output.
